description: 3.3 V to 5 V logic buffer; DIP-14
notes: U1; use the through-hole N package. At 5 V supply its input HIGH threshold is 2.0 V, suitable for the Nano's 3.3 V outputs. Two channels carry data and clock. Datasheet: https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/sn74ahct125.pdf
R3/R4; one in series with each buffered data/clock output. Cut tape; listed cost is for two at CAD0.16 each. These are signal resistors, not LED power-current limiters.
R1/R2; input pull-downs for data and clock. Cut tape; listed cost is for two at CAD0.16 each. Reuse suitable resistors already owned.

description: 100 nF 50 V X7R radial ceramic capacitor
notes: C1; bypass U1's 5 V supply to common ground, close to the chip. Nonpolarized; 5 mm lead pitch. Cut tape.

C2; positive to LED +5 V, negative/striped lead to common GND. 10 mm body diameter, 5 mm lead pitch; fits i43/i45. Buy one cut-tape piece. Manufacturer dimensions: https://industrial.panasonic.com/ww/products/pt/aluminum-cap-lead/models/EEUFC1A102B

description: Breadboard-friendly 2.1 mm DC barrel jack; thin-pin type
notes: J0; for the LED/buffer 5 V feed. Centre positive b58, sleeve ground b60, switched sleeve d59 unused; opening faces board bottom. description: USB-A to 5.5 x 2.1 mm centre-positive 5 V barrel cable
manufacturer_part: X2 Robotics 0939; equivalent connection to Adafruit 2697
notes: One cable for the LED/buffer branch, separate from the Nano USB cable. Canadian listing specifies 1 m, 24 AWG and centre-positive 5 V; suitable for this short-strip prototype. Adafruit 2697 is another option: https://www.adafruit.com/product/2697 . Choose only one. PSU USB connector remains to be confirmed; this cable assumes USB-A. Do not buy a 9 V/12 V USB booster cable.

Nano powered through its own USB socket. USB at top, headers c1-c15 and g1-g15. D11 data, D13 clock. Leave VIN/c15 and 5V-VUSB/c12 unconnected to the breadboard supply; keep the common-ground jumper at a14.

description: USB cable for the Nano 33 IoT micro-USB socket
notes: One separate power/data cable to the Nano USB socket; use a data-capable cable for programming. It is additional to the USB-to-barrel cable for J0.

For standalone PoC use two USB outputs with at least 1 A combined rated capacity and adequate per-port ratings: one to Nano, one through the barrel cable to J0. Alternatively power Nano from PC USB and LEDs/buffer from the separate 5 V USB PSU. Grounds join; do not join the independent +5 V feeds through Nano headers. Check the actual PSU label and USB connector. Its current rating is available capacity, not current forced into the load.

description: 64-row solderless breadboard and suitable jumper wires
notes: Standard a-e and f-j terminal banks, separated by the centre gap. All components are plug-in; power rails are unused in the drawing. Only a physically short LED section belongs on these power contacts.

description: APA102 LED strip; 160 inches planned, 60 LEDs per metre
notes: Start with 1-5 physically connected pixels; five pixels are about 8.3 cm and allow a conservative 0.30 A LED budget at 60 mA/pixel, plus the Nano/buffer on their branches. Connect the INPUT end: a40 GND, a41 CI, a42 DI, a43 +5 V. CO/DO are downstream outputs. Cut only at marked pads.

description: Power distribution and supply sized for the complete APA102 strip
notes: 160 inches = 4.064 m, about 244 pixels at 60/m. A conservative 60 mA/pixel planning value gives about 14.6 A at 5 V before controller draw; actual variant/current must be checked. Full-strip power needs suitable external wiring and injection, not the breadboard or Nano USB path. Guide: https://learn.adafruit.com/adafruit-dotstar-leds/power-and-connections

description: Multimeter and suitable plug-in strip connector or leads
notes: Verify J0 polarity and the strip input pad order before connection. The strip's existing connector type and pitch are not confirmed, so no mating connector is guessed in this order list. A cut strip section may require soldered leads or a correctly matched solderless strip clip.
